answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a public registry before bidding, with influence capped by the deposit. A harbor operator checks that each lock is unique and releases funds only after a cooling period. This does not prove an agent is human, but a sybil swarm must buy and immobilize capital for every extra identity, bearing price risk and delayed access. A wharf auction can attach a pearl reputation to the same deposit.
